body:
Habr article automation now reads complete editor documents, exports exact viewer/editor/source diffs, and prepares every repository revision for upload. Long CodeMirror documents retain offscreen text and final whitespace; visual-editor extraction preserves figures, code, and formulas instead of mistaking embedded widgets for the article.

Fixes #57. Addresses the [selected/latest draft review](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory/pull/58#issuecomment-5995102556) and [request to audit every draft](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory/pull/58#issuecomment-5998114580).

- Use the latest verified browser-commander **0.25.0**, with Playwright **1.63.0**, Puppeteer **25.12.0**, persistent login, and explicit bundled/installed-browser selection.
- Support `--draft latest`, named draft/archive versions, flat `article.md`, version directories, numbered sections, indexes, and standalone files. The latest source includes all ten sections: **153,542 bytes, 13 figures, 26 code blocks, and 159 formulas**. All repository assets exist. Markdown image rewriting handles references, spaces, parentheses, and titles while preserving code examples.
- Download public/editor Markdown and print/export complete unified diffs, hashes, and separate exact/normalized equality. JSON output keeps verbose browser diagnostics on stderr. `sync` retains the public/editor equality gate; `--force` acknowledges a reviewed mismatch without enabling writes.
- Keep `apply`/`sync` dry by default. `prefill` changes a disposable copy of the login profile with HTTP writes and WebSockets blocked across all tabs, existing service workers excluded, and new registration disabled. Closing it discards unsent localStorage autosaves. Only `--write` permits Habr's draft autosave traffic; no save, settings, submit, or publish buttons are clicked.
- Use Habr's visual-editor Markdown clipboard parser only with `--allow-wysiwyg-paste`; re-extract the result, retain before/after snapshots, and return exit 1 with a patch for remaining differences. Original/source recovery files survive failed parsing.
- Add browser regression CI, reusable baseline/safety experiments, complete [usage documentation](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory/blob/issue-57-bdfa795fee8c/docs/habr-article-sync.md), and a [case study mapping every requirement to implementation and evidence](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory/blob/issue-57-bdfa795fee8c/docs/case-studies/issue-57/README.md).

Current `main` is merged, package conflicts are resolved, and the PDF automation and revision-release trigger are retained.

### Reproduction and validation

The initial seven regressions covered truncated/short documents, captured semantic content, embedded editor selection, missing patches/draft assembly, and unsafe boolean values. The continuation also reproduced unsupported archive/flat inputs, image corruption, invented final newlines, localStorage prefill leakage, unguarded new tabs, ineffective service-worker options, missing recovery snapshots, and verbose diagnostics corrupting JSON reports.

Run `node experiments/issue-57/reproduce-cli-baseline.mjs` to verify that the previous CLI fails the localStorage/recovery tests. Run `node experiments/issue-57/new-tab-guard-probe.mjs --baseline` to observe the previous tab guard allowing a POST; omit `--baseline` to verify zero writes. Both probes use finite local fixtures and retain the original commit history.

Verified locally with Node.js 22.23.3:

- `npm run test:habr-sync`: **27 passed**. Every revision round-trips exactly through a real virtualized CodeMirror editor. Local MarkdownIt/KaTeX visual extraction retains every figure/code/formula across all four revisions. The supplied Habr capture retains all 61 opaque formulas. CLI tests verify guarded prefill, explicit autosaves, both sync diffs, new-tab blocking, login-cookie retention, worker registration prevention, recovery files, and valid JSON with verbose tracing.
- `npm run test:web-capture`: **19 passed**; `npm test`: **222 live checks passed** across the three archived articles.
- `PDF_NO_SANDBOX=1 npm run test:pdf`: **8 passed**; all four PDFs build and validate after the shared browser upgrade, including the latest 52-page article.
- Clean `npm ci`, syntax checks, file-size checks, and `git diff --check`: passed. Archived TAP evidence retains intentional whitespace through a narrowly scoped Git attribute.
- Live CLI public download of article 1018142: **54,384 bytes**, unchanged SHA-256 recorded in the case study. No authenticated live writes were performed.

CI passed on final commit `f8f8d45`: [Habr and web-capture regressions](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory/actions/runs/37447217812), [all PDF builds and checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory/actions/runs/37447217873), and [formal verification workflow/file checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory/actions/runs/37447217828). Lean/Rocq jobs were skipped because their files are unchanged; publication runs only after a push to `main`.

`npm run test:capture` has **23 passing checks and one existing failure** at `scripts/test-capture-quality.mjs:355`: it expects a log phrase absent from the unchanged capture script. The same failure is documented in [main's issue 59 baseline](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-theory/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-59/capture-baseline.txt); current output is preserved in this case study. ffmpeg-dependent video checks were skipped locally.

### Usage and verification limits

After `npm ci`, Chromium installation, and manual `login --headed`:

```bash
npm run habr:sync -- download-edit \
  --url https://habr.com/ru/article/edit/1018142 --draft latest \
  --output .browser/edit.md --diff-output .browser/editor-source.diff --headed

npm run habr:sync -- prefill \
  --url https://habr.com/ru/article/edit/1018142 --draft latest \
  --headed --keep-open --allow-wysiwyg-paste
```

Use `apply --write` or `sync --write` when remote draft autosaves are intended. Authenticated live prefill, Habr's clipboard normalization for the full article, and durable server persistence require a local Habr account/profile. Local visual conversion tests establish semantic preservation; exact buffer equality and server persistence remain separate checks. The default autosave wait and optional open browser allow manual saved-status inspection.
